title: Packing k^2-c unit squares: a lower bound of order k^{1/3} for the deficiency (preprint)
description: Licences in this single record: the preprint (paper/paper.pdf, paper/paper.tex) is licensed under CC BY 4.0; the programs (code/) under the MIT License, which is the licence shown for the record. Preprint with programs. Let M(k) be the largest number of unit squares in [0,k]^2 that are pairwise disjoint as closed sets; then s(k^2-c) = k exactly when c < k^2 - M(k). The preprint proves k^2 - M(k) > 10^-4 sqrt(k) for every integer k in [10^8, 2.5*10^15], k^2 - M(k) > 7*10^-5 sqrt(k) for k in [2.5*10^15, 3.5*10^17], k^2 - M(k) > 0.06 k^{1/3} for every integer k >= 3.5*10^17, and liminf (k^2 - M(k))/k^{1/3} >= 0.06285. For every k >= 4.62*10^12 these bounds exceed the bound 0.1 k^{1/4} of the previous preprint on the k^{1/4} bound. The proof uses Sections 3-8 of that preprint and Lemmas 4.13 and 4.15 of the paper 'Packing k^2-c unit squares: s(k^2-c)=k for all large k' (version 1.2); the constants also rely on its computer-assisted Lemma 4.10, whose box computations have not yet been reproduced by an independent implementation (without it: 0.05 k^{1/3} from 3.39*10^17 on, and 0.05229). Includes three independently written programs that check the table of the proof in interval and exact rational arithmetic. Status: checked only by AI-based reviews, computer programs and a numerical test on scaled analogues; not peer reviewed. Use of AI: developed with extensive assistance from Claude (Anthropic), including the proofs, the text and the programs; the author takes full responsibility.
